messages:
maria_support: Hey team — customer (acct: acme-inc, org_id: org_83) reporting a spike of 429s over the last hour after they enabled multi-region failover. They say their client started getting 429s and inflated retry traffic. Sample req IDs: req_0a1b2c3d, req_0f3e2d1c. They sent us a short repro with a looped client that retries on 429. Can someone look at cross-region routing behavior and quota exhaustion?

robin_sre: Thanks — can you paste the exact response headers from one of the failing requests? Need X-Region, X-Fallback, X-Quota, X-RateLimit-* if present. Also helpful: is this Hosted API or Dedicated?

maria_support: Hosted. Here's a raw response captured by the customer: ```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2025 15:22:10 GMT
X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d
X-Region: eu-west-1
X-Fallback-Region: us-west-2
X-Client-Quota: 600/min
Retry-After: 10
Content-Type: application/json
``` They also included the client loop: ```for i in range(0,1000): resp = api.call(...); if resp.status==429: time.sleep(0.2); continue```

anya_engineer: quick notes — 'X-Fallback-Region' header in the response indicates the request was routed to eu-west first then fell back to us-west. If eu-west capacity is saturated we do a fallback. Need to check routing logs for the customer to see if they hit per-region per-customer quota or global throttle.

robin_sre: I'm pulling routing traces now. Command I'm using: ```SELECT * FROM routing_logs WHERE request_id IN ('req_0a1b2c3d','req_0f3e2d1c');``` Preliminary: eu-west pool reached 98% GPU utilization around 15:20 UTC, several in-flight requests overflowed and were routed to fallback us-west which has a separate per-customer burst quota. The customer exceeded their us-west burst credits causing 429s there.

maria_support: Customer mentions unexpected billing spike as well — they see lots of rewound tokens because client retried whole requests. Is there an accounting rule for retries?

billing-bot: FYI — retries that result in a served response are billable. If the request is accepted by our runtime and tokens generated, the invoice records the served tokens. Re-executed retries that reach model tokens count toward usage.

ops-oncall: Two immediate mitigations: 1) advise customer to implement exponential backoff (e.g., jitter, doubling) instead of tight loops; 2) temporarily bump the customer's regional burst for us-west while we investigate so they don't see hard 429s. I can apply a +200 burst credit for 30 minutes if you want.

maria_support: They want a quick fix now — please apply the burst. Also confirm what caused eu-west saturation (was it noisy neighbor or scheduled job?).

robin_sre: I checked cluster events — there was a scheduled training job mis-labeled 'dev/nlp-embed' that spiked memory and caused the autoscaler to delay pod spin-up for ~6 minutes. That caused temporary reduction in inference capacity. So fallback behavior is expected. However, routing policy should have honored per-region fallback budget and not overflow us-west quota so quickly — I'm filing a follow-up ticket on routing policy enforcement.

anya_engineer: Routing policy nuance: default is "fallback-allow" which routes to fallback when primary capacity < threshold. We have a per-region per-customer burst bucket (ref: RB-001) and a global fallback cooldown. If fallback causes immediate throttle in the target region we should attempt other compatible model variants or queue (depending on customer's SLO). For Hosted customers without reserved capacity, fallback can produce this cascade.

robin_sre: Action items I'm doing now: - increase customer us-west burst +200 for 30m (doing it) - tag the routing traces and attach to internal incident - run synthetic repro from inside our eu-west pool to verify autoscaler/resizing - follow up with infra team on the mislabeled training job

ops-oncall: Applied burst +200 to acct org_83 for region us-west-2, expires in 30m. Monitor dashboard: https://console/redwood/orgs/org_83/usage?region=us-west-2

maria_support: Customer confirmed 429 rate dropped within ~2 mins of the burst add. They still want a long-term solution: avoid cross-region throttle cascades and get a clear explanation for the billing spike.

robin_sre: For the billing spike, short explanation: retries that hit a second region and are accepted will be billed twice (original attempt + retry) unless the first attempt was rejected before token generation. Recommend we: 1) document best-practices for customers on backoff & idempotency, 2) add a billing note explaining retry accounting, 3) explore server-side dedupe for retried request-ids (but that's a bigger product change).

anya_engineer: Long-term engineering suggestions: - Make fallback policy prefer "hold-and-queue" for customers above a billing threshold instead of immediate cross-region fallback. - Add a circuit-breaker that delays fallback if fallback-target burst usage > 50% of bucket. - Improve our client SDKs with built-in exponential backoff presets and an example for multi-region setups.

maria_support: Customer asks for repro steps we can give them to reproduce safely (so they can test our fix). Any recommended safe repro?

robin_sre: Safe repro (non-billing-inflating): 1) Set low concurrency (e.g., 4 concurrent clients) and relatively few total requests (200). 2) Configure client to stop retrying after 2 attempts, exponential backoff with jitter: ```if resp.status==429: sleep = random.uniform(0,0.5)*(2**attempt)``` 3) Run with primary region preference = eu-west to trigger fallback logic. 4) Share request-ids back to support. This will let us observe routing without generating huge token counts.

ops-oncall: Also add a note: run repro during a maintenance window and notify support so we can watch dashboards in real-time (latency, queue lengths, per-region burst usage).

maria_support: Will share this with customer and ask them to run the safe repro. Also asked infra to prevent the training job from running in prod pools.

robin_sre: I'll open internal ticket SRT-5421 to track: root cause (scheduled training job), short-term mitigation (burst bump), medium-term changes (routing cooldowns, circuit-breaker), and docs updates. Assigning to anya_engineer for feature follow-ups.

anya_engineer: Got it — I'll own the routing-policy tasks and SDK backoff examples. ETA: initial design doc in 5 business days.

maria_support: Thanks everyone — I'll send the customer the safe repro and confirm when they test. Closing the immediate support thread but keeping it monitored until the ticket is resolved. :white_check_mark:

billing-bot: NOTE: created billing ticket BILL-911 for the customer's spike and marked it for investigation; attach invoice snapshots if they request credits.

robin_sre: Follow-up — after the autoscaler fix the eu-west pool returned to normal capacity and no further fallbacks were observed. I'll update SRT-5421 with traces and the autoscaler log excerpt.```
